concept.title: Reviewing information reported after claimant’s reports have been processed

conbody.p: When a client comes forward to correct previously provided information or provide previously omitted information, the agent determines if the information can be considered an error correction or if it must be referred to Integrity to be considered under the voluntary disclosure policy.

The voluntary disclosure policy may apply if the client is aware that misinformation resulted in an inappropriate payment of benefits and is attempting to correct this situation. Unless specified otherwise, it is presumed that in providing the information, the client is in agreement that benefits were not payable.

To determine if the new information can be considered an error correction or must be referred to Integrity, the agent refers to Determining if an issue must be referred to Integrity . Determining if an issue must be referred to Integrity

ul.li: If the original statement is received on an electronic claimant’s report, use the date the claimant’s report is processed (if unassisted) or the date it is successfully completed (if assisted).
If the original statement is received on a paper claimant’s report, use the date preceding the day the claimant’s report is processed.
If the original statement is received on any other paper document, use the date the paper document is received.
If the original statement is received verbally, use the date of the verbal statement, as shown on the SROC or WI.
If the client is exempted from completing claimant’s reports, use the date after the last payment was issued.
If the request for correction is received on a paper document, use the date the paper document is received.
If the request for correction is received verbally, use the date of the verbal request, as shown on the SROC or WI.

conbody.p: Any request for correction submitted more than 6 weeks after the original statement was made is not considered a simple error correction. Consequently, the Voluntary disclosure procedures must be applied.
